rows.cast: Clive Brook, Diana Wynyard, Helen Vinson
rows.extract: Let's Try Again is a 1934 American melodrama film starring Clive Brook. It was known in Britain as Marriage Symphony.

rows.title: The Life of Vergie Winters
rows.cast: Ann Harding, John Boles
rows.extract: The Life of Vergie Winters is a 1934 American Pre-Code film, starring Ann Harding and John Boles.

rows.title: Lighting Bill
rows.cast: Jay Wilsey, Alma Rayford

rows.title: Lightning Strikes Twice
rows.cast: Ben Lyon, Thelma Todd
rows.extract: Lightning Strikes Twice is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Ben Holmes from a screenplay by Joseph A. Fields and John Grey. It stars Ben Lyon, Thelma Todd, and Pert Kelton. A print is held by the Library of Congress.

rows.title: Limehouse Blues
rows.cast: George Raft, Jean Parker, Anna May Wong
rows.extract: Limehouse Blues is a 1934 American crime film, directed by Alexander Hall. The film is set in the Limehouse district in the East End of London and its Chinatown. Among the stars of the film were George Raft and Anna May Wong. The film is named after the song "Limehouse Blues".

rows.title: The Line-Up
rows.cast: William Gargan, Marian Nixon, John Miljan
rows.extract: The Line-Up is a 1934 American crime film directed by Howard Higgin and starring William Gargan, Marian Nixon and Paul Hurst.

rows.title: Little Man, What Now?
rows.cast: Margaret Sullavan, Douglass Montgomery, Alan Hale
rows.extract: Little Man, What Now? is a 1934 pre-Code American drama film directed by Frank Borzage and starring Margaret Sullavan. It is based on the novel of the same name by Hans Fallada. The novel had been turned into a German film the previous year. The film was a box-office disappointment for Universal.

rows.title: Little Men
rows.cast: Ralph Morgan, Erin O'Brien-Moore
rows.extract: Little Men is a 1934 American feature film based on Louisa May Alcott's 1871 novel Little Men, starring Ralph Morgan and Erin O'Brien-Moore, directed by Phil Rosen, and was released by Mascot Pictures. Alcott wrote Little Men in response to her prior novel, Little Women, hoping to achieve the same l

rows.title: The Little Minister
rows.cast: Katharine Hepburn, John Beal
rows.extract: The Little Minister is a 1934 American drama film starring Katharine Hepburn and directed by Richard Wallace. The screenplay by Jane Murfin, Sarah Y. Mason, and Victor Heerman is based on the 1891 novel and subsequent 1897 play of the same title by J.M. Barrie. The picture was the fifth film adaptat

rows.title: Little Miss Marker
rows.cast: Adolphe Menjou, Shirley Temple, Charles Bickford
rows.extract: Little Miss Marker is an American Pre-Code 1934 comedy-drama film directed by Alexander Hall. It was written by William R. Lipman, Sam Hellman, and Gladys Lehman after a 1932 short story of the same name by Damon Runyon. It stars Shirley Temple, Adolphe Menjou and Dorothy Dell in a story about a you

rows.title: Long Lost Father
rows.cast: John Barrymore, Helen Chandler
rows.extract: Long Lost Father is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film starring John Barrymore, Helen Chandler, Donald Cook, Alan Mowbray, and Doris Lloyd. It was directed by Ernest B. Schoedsack. It was based on a 1933 novel of the same title by the British writer Gladys Stern.

rows.title: Looking for Trouble
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Constance Cummings
rows.extract: Looking for Trouble is a 1934 American Pre-Code crime film directed by William A. Wellman and starring Spencer Tracy, Jack Oakie and Constance Cummings. After he is rejected by a woman, a man leaves his safe job and joins a gang that robs banks. The film features actual stock earthquake footage.

rows.title: Lost in the Stratosphere
rows.cast: William Cagney, June Collyer
rows.extract: Lost in the Stratosphere is a 1934 American aviation drama film directed by Melville W. Brown and starring William Cagney, Edward J. Nugent, and June Collyer. In one of his few roles in front of the cameras, Cagney was the lookalike younger brother of James Cagney.

rows.title: A Lost Lady
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Frank Morgan, Ricardo Cortez
rows.extract: A Lost Lady is a 1934 American drama film directed by Alfred E. Green and starring by Barbara Stanwyck, Frank Morgan, and Ricardo Cortez. Based on the 1923 novel A Lost Lady by Willa Cather, with a screenplay by Gene Markey and Kathryn Scola, the film is about a woman whose fiancé is murdered by his

rows.title: The Lost Patrol
rows.cast: Victor McLaglen, Wallace Ford, Boris Karloff
rows.extract: The Lost Patrol is a 1934 American pre-Code war film by RKO, directed and produced by John Ford, with Merian C. Cooper as executive producer and Cliff Reid as associate producer from a screenplay by Dudley Nichols from the 1927 novel Patrol by Philip MacDonald. Max Steiner provided the Oscar-nominat

rows.title: Love Birds
rows.cast: Slim Summerville, ZaSu Pitts, Mickey Rooney
rows.extract: Love Birds is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by William A. Seiter and written by Doris Anderson, Henry Myers, and Tom Reed. The film stars Slim Summerville, ZaSu Pitts, Mickey Rooney, Frederick Burton, Emmett Vogan, and Dorothy Christy. The film was released on May 4, 1934, by Univers

rows.title: The Love Captive
rows.cast: Gloria Stuart, Nils Asther
rows.extract: The Love Captive is a 1934 American drama film directed by Max Marcin and written by Karen DeWolf, adapted from Marcin's play of the same name. The film stars Gloria Stuart, Nils Asther, Paul Kelly, Alan Dinehart, Renee Gadd, and Russ Brown. The film was released on June 7, 1934, by Universal Pictur

rows.title: Love Past Thirty
rows.cast: Aileen Pringle, Theodore von Eltz, Phyllis Barry
rows.extract: Love Past Thirty is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by Vin Moore and starring Aileen Pringle, Theodore von Eltz and Phyllis Barry.

rows.title: Love Time
rows.cast: Pat Paterson, Nils Asther
rows.extract: Love Time is a 1934 American historical drama film directed by James Tinling and starring Pat Paterson, Nils Asther and Herbert Mundin. The film was released on September 21, 1934, by Fox Film Corporation. The film is a romanticized biopic of the nineteenth century Austrian composer Franz Schubert,

rows.title: The Lucky Texan
rows.cast: John Wayne, Barbara Sheldon, George "Gabby" Hayes
rows.extract: The Lucky Texan is a 1934 American Lonestar Films B-movie Western film featuring John Wayne, Barbara Sheldon, Gabby Hayes, and the legendary stuntman and actor Yakima Canutt. It was written and directed by Robert N. Bradbury. It also contains a rare appearance by "Gabby" Hayes without a beard and in

rows.title: Madame DuBarry
rows.cast: Dolores del Río, Victor Jory, Osgood Perkins
rows.extract: Madame DuBarry is a 1934 American historical film directed by William Dieterle and starring Dolores del Río, Reginald Owen, Victor Jory and Osgood Perkins. The film portrays the life of Madame Du Barry, the last mistress of King Louis XV of France. While this film does not serve accuracy to Madame D

rows.title: Madame Spy
rows.cast: Fay Wray, Nils Asther, Edward Arnold
rows.extract: Madame Spy is a 1934 American adventure film directed by Karl Freund and starring Fay Wray, Oscar Apfel, Edward Arnold and Nils Asther. The film was produced and distributed by Universal Pictures. It is a remake of the 1932 film Under False Flag which was produced by Deutsche Universal, the German s

rows.title: The Man from Hell
rows.cast: Reb Russell, Fred Kohler
rows.extract: The Man from Hell is a 1934 American Western film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Reb Russell, Fred Kohler and George 'Gabby' Hayes.

rows.title: The Man from Utah
rows.cast: John Wayne, Polly Ann Young, George "Gabby" Hayes
rows.extract: The Man from Utah is a 1934 pre-Code Monogram Western film starring John Wayne, Polly Ann Young and the stuntman/actor Yakima Canutt. It was written by Lindsley Parsons and directed by Robert N. Bradbury. Wayne has a "singing cowboy scene" in the film, wherein his voice is dubbed.

rows.title: Man of Two Worlds
rows.cast: Elissa Landi, Francis Lederer
rows.extract: Man of Two Worlds is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by J. Walter Ruben and starring Francis Lederer, Elissa Landi and Henry Stephenson.

rows.title: The Man Trailer
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Cecilia Parker
rows.extract: The Man Trailer is a 1934 American pre-Code western film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Buck Jones and Cecilia Parker. It was a remake of the 1930 film The Lone Rider which had also starred Jones. It was shot at the Iverson Ranch.

rows.title: The Man Who Reclaimed His Head
rows.cast: Claude Rains, Joan Bennett, Lionel Atwill
rows.extract: The Man Who Reclaimed His Head is a 1934 American drama film directed by Edward Ludwig and written by Jean Bart and Samuel Ornitz. The film stars Claude Rains, Joan Bennett, Lionel Atwill, Juanita Quigley, Henry O'Neill and Henry Armetta. The film was released on December 24, 1934, by Universal Pict

rows.title: The Man with Two Faces
rows.cast: Edward G. Robinson, Mary Astor, Ricardo Cortez
rows.extract: The Man with Two Faces is an American drama film directed by Archie Mayo, and starring Edward G. Robinson and Mary Astor. The supporting cast features Ricardo Cortez, Louis Calhern, Mae Clarke, and David Landau. The story was adapted by Tom Reed and Niven Busch from the play The Dark Tower by George

rows.title: A Man's Game
rows.cast: Tim McCoy, Evalyn Knapp
rows.extract: A Man's Game is a 1934 American drama film directed by D. Ross Lederman. Released by Columbia Pictures, the film stars Tim McCoy, Evalyn Knapp and Ward Bond.

rows.title: Managed Money
rows.cast: Junior Coghlan, Shirley Temple
rows.extract: Managed Money is a 1934 short comedy film directed by Charles Lamont. The film stars Frank Coghlan Jr. and Shirley Temple. It was also known as Frolics of Youth and Measured Money. This was the second film in which Temple starred as Mary Lou. The film tells the story of Sonny and Sid prospecting for

rows.title: Mandalay
rows.cast: Kay Francis, Ricardo Cortez, Warner Oland
rows.extract: Mandalay is a 1934 American pre Code drama film directed by Michael Curtiz and written by Austin Parker and Charles Kenyon based on a story by Paul Hervey Fox. The film stars Kay Francis, Ricardo Cortez, Warner Oland and Lyle Talbot, and features Ruth Donnelly and Reginald Owen.

rows.title: Manhattan Love Song
rows.cast: Robert Armstrong, Dixie Lee
rows.extract: Manhattan Love Song is a 1934 American pre-Code film directed by Leonard Fields.

rows.title: Manhattan Melodrama
rows.cast: Clark Gable, William Powell, Myrna Loy
rows.extract: Manhattan Melodrama is a 1934 American pre-Code crime film, produced by MGM, directed by W. S. Van Dyke, and starring Clark Gable, William Powell, and Myrna Loy. The movie also provided one of Mickey Rooney's earliest film roles. The film is based on a story by Arthur Caesar, who won the Academy Awa

rows.title: Maniac
rows.cast: Bill Woods, Horace Carpenter
rows.extract: Maniac is a 1934 American black-and-white exploitation horror film directed by Dwain Esper and written by Hildagarde Stadie, Esper's wife, as a loose adaptation of the 1843 Edgar Allan Poe story "The Black Cat", with references to his "Murders in the Rue Morgue". Esper and Stadie also made the 1936

rows.title: Many Happy Returns
rows.cast: Gracie Allen, George Burns, George Barbier
rows.extract: Many Happy Returns is a 1934 American pre-Code Paramount Pictures comedy film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and starring Gracie Allen, George Burns, and George Barbier.

rows.title: Marie Galante
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Ketti Gallian, Ned Sparks
rows.extract: Marie Galante is a 1934 American film directed by Henry King, starring Ketti Gallian and Spencer Tracy, adapted from a French novel by Jacques Deval. Later in the same year the novel was adapted into a French musical titled Marie Galante, with book and lyrics by Jacques Deval and music by Kurt Weill

rows.title: The Marines Are Coming
rows.cast: William Haines, Conrad Nagel, Esther Ralston
rows.extract: The Marines Are Coming is a 1934 American action drama film directed by David Howard and starring William Haines, Conrad Nagel and Esther Ralston. It was produced and distributed by the independent Mascot Pictures. It was the final film acting role of Haines who had a major success in the 1928 film

rows.title: Marrying Widows
rows.cast: Judith Allen, Johnny Mack Brown, Minna Gombell
rows.extract: Marrying Widows is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Sam Newfield and starring Judith Allen, Johnny Mack Brown and Minna Gombell.

rows.title: Massacre
rows.cast: Richard Barthelmess, Ann Dvorak
rows.extract: Massacre is a 1934 American drama film directed by Alan Crosland. The film stars Richard Barthelmess and Ann Dvorak as its Native American protagonists, and also features Charles Middleton, Sidney Toler, Claire Dodd and Clarence Muse.

rows.title: The Meanest Gal in Town
rows.cast: ZaSu Pitts, El Brendel
rows.extract: The Meanest Gal in Town is a 1934 American Pre-Code romantic comedy, directed by Russell Mack from a screenplay written by Richard Schayer, Russell Mack, and H. W. Hanemann, and starring Zasu Pitts, El Brendel, Pert Kelton, and James Gleason.

rows.title: Melody in Spring
rows.cast: Lanny Ross, Charlie Ruggles, Mary Boland, Ann Sothern
rows.extract: Melody in Spring is a 1934 American pre-Code musical film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and written by Benn W. Levy, Frank Leon Smith, and Jane Storm. The film stars Lanny Ross, Charlie Ruggles, Mary Boland, Ann Sothern, George Meeker, and Herman Bing. The film was released on April 20, 1934, by Para

rows.title: Men in White
rows.cast: Clark Gable, Jean Hersholt, Myrna Loy
rows.extract: Men in White is a 1934 pre-Code film starring Clark Gable and Myrna Loy, and directed by Ryszard Bolesławski. The story is loosely based on the Sidney Kingsley Pulitzer-Prize-winning play of the same name. Due to suggestions of illicit romance and abortion, the film was frequently cut. The Legion of

rows.title: Men of the Night
rows.cast: Bruce Cabot, Judith Allen
rows.extract: Men of the Night is a 1934 American drama film written and directed by Lambert Hillyer, which stars Bruce Cabot, Judith Allen, and Ward Bond.

rows.title: Menace
rows.cast: Gertrude Michael, Paul Cavanagh
rows.extract: Menace is a 1934 American mystery film directed by Ralph Murphy.

rows.title: The Merry Frinks
rows.cast: Aline MacMahon, Guy Kibbee
rows.extract: The Merry Frinks is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Alfred E. Green and starring Aline MacMahon, Guy Kibbee and Hugh Herbert. It is also known by the alternative title of Happy Family.

rows.title: The Merry Widow
rows.cast: Jeanette MacDonald, Maurice Chevalier, Edward Everett Horton
rows.extract: The Merry Widow is a 1934 film adaptation of the 1905 operetta of the same name by Franz Lehár. The film was directed and produced by Ernst Lubitsch starring Maurice Chevalier and Jeanette MacDonald with a supporting cast featuring Edward Everett Horton, Una Merkel, Sterling Holloway, Donald Meek, J

rows.title: Midnight
rows.cast: Sidney Fox, Margaret Wycherly, Humphrey Bogart
rows.extract: Midnight is a 1934 American drama film, the first directed by Chester Erskine, and starring Sidney Fox, O.P. Heggie, Henry Hull and Margaret Wycherly. It was based on a Theatre Guild play with the same name by Paul and Claire Sifton. The film was produced for Universal and was shot on a modest budge

rows.title: Midnight Alibi
rows.cast: Richard Barthelmess, Ann Dvorak
rows.extract: Midnight Alibi is a 1934 pre-Code crime comedy-drama directed by Alan Crosland, produced by First National Pictures, distributed by Warner Bros. and starring Richard Barthelmess. Midnight Alibi is an adaptation of Damon Runyon's 1933 short story The Old Doll's House.

rows.title: The Mighty Barnum
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Adolphe Menjou, Virginia Bruce
rows.extract: The Mighty Barnum is a 1934 film starring Wallace Beery as P.T. Barnum. The movie was written by Gene Fowler and Bess Meredyth, adapted from their play of the same name, and directed by Walter Lang. Beery had played Barnum four years earlier in A Lady's Morals, a highly fictionalized biography of si

rows.title: Mills of the Gods
rows.cast: May Robson, Fay Wray
rows.extract: The Mills of the Gods is an American silent film. It was the first three-reel "feature" directed by Ralph Ince; production company Vitagraph entrusted him with this longer project after being impressed by his work on the two-reel Double Danger.

rows.title: Million Dollar Baby
rows.cast: Arline Judge, Ray Walker, Jeanette Loff
rows.extract: Million Dollar Baby is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Joseph Santley and starring Arline Judge, Ray Walker and Jimmy Fay.

rows.title: Million Dollar Ransom
rows.cast: Phillips Holmes, Edward Arnold
rows.extract: Million Dollar Ransom is a 1934 American drama film directed by Murray Roth and written by William R. Lipman and Ben Ryan. The film stars Phillips Holmes, Edward Arnold, Mary Carlisle, Wini Shaw, Andy Devine and Robert Gleckler. The film was released on September 1, 1934, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Miss Fane's Baby Is Stolen
rows.cast: Dorothea Wieck, Alice Brady
rows.extract: Miss Fane's Baby Is Stolen is a 1934 pre-Code American comedy-drama film, starring Dorothea Wieck, Alice Brady, and Baby LeRoy, written by Adela Rogers St. Johns and Jane Storm from a novel and story by Rupert Hughes, and directed by Alexander Hall. The events depicted in the film were allegedly bas

rows.title: Money Means Nothing
rows.cast: Wallace Ford, Gloria Shea
rows.extract: Money Means Nothing is a 1934 American drama film, directed by Christy Cabanne. It stars Wallace Ford, Gloria Shea, and Edgar Kennedy, and was released on June 14, 1934.

rows.title: Monte Carlo Nights
rows.cast: Mary Brian, John Darrow, Gabby Hayes
rows.extract: Monte Carlo Nights is a 1934 American pre-Code film directed by William Nigh.

rows.title: The Most Precious Thing in Life
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, Jean Arthur
rows.extract: The Most Precious Thing in Life is a 1934 American pre-Code film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Richard Cromwell, Jean Arthur, Donald Cook, Anita Louise, and Mary Forbes.

rows.title: Moulin Rouge
rows.cast: Constance Bennett, Franchot Tone, Tullio Carminati
rows.extract: Moulin Rouge is an American pre-Code musical film released on January 19, 1934, by United Artists, starring Constance Bennett and Franchot Tone. It contained the songs "Coffee in the Morning and Kisses in the Night", and "Boulevard of Broken Dreams" with music by Harry Warren and lyrics by Al Dubin.

rows.title: Murder at the Vanities
rows.cast: Victor McLaglen, Carl Brisson
rows.extract: Murder at the Vanities is a 1934 American Pre-Code musical film based on the 1933 Broadway show with music by Victor Young. It was released by Paramount Pictures. It was directed by Mitchell Leisen, stars Victor McLaglen, Carl Brisson, Jack Oakie, Kitty Carlisle, Gertrude Michael, Toby Wing, and Jes

rows.title: Murder in the Clouds
rows.cast: Lyle Talbot, Ann Dvorak
rows.extract: Murder in the Clouds is a 1934 American action film dealing with aviation. The film stars Lyle Talbot and Ann Dvorak, and is directed by D. Ross Lederman. Although standard formula "B" film fare, it was notable as the screenplay and original story was written by Dore Schary as a freelance writer, du

rows.title: Murder in the Private Car
rows.cast: Charles Ruggles, Una Merkel
rows.extract: Murder in the Private Car is a 1934 American pre-Code mystery romance film starring Mary Carlisle, Charles Ruggles and Una Merkel. Directed by Harry Beaumont, the production is based on the play The Rear Car by Edward E. Rose. David Townsend was the film's art director.

rows.title: Murder in Trinidad
rows.cast: Nigel Bruce, Heather Angel
rows.extract: Murder in Trinidad is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Louis King and starring Nigel Bruce, Heather Angel, Victor Jory, and Murray Kinnell.

rows.title: Mrs. Wiggs of the Cabbage Patch
rows.cast: W. C. Fields, Pauline Lord, ZaSu Pitts
rows.extract: Mrs. Wiggs of the Cabbage Patch is a 1934 American comedy-drama film, directed by Norman Taurog, and is based on the 1904 Broadway play by Anne Crawford Flexner, which itself is taken from the novel of the same name by Alice Hegan Rice. The film stars Broadway stage actress Pauline Lord, and is one

rows.title: Murder on the Blackboard
rows.cast: Edna May Oliver, James Gleason
rows.extract: Murder on the Blackboard is a 1934 American pre-Code mystery/comedy film starring Edna May Oliver as schoolteacher Hildegarde Withers and James Gleason as Police Inspector Oscar Piper. Together, they investigate a murder at Withers' school. It was based on the novel of the same name by Stuart Palmer

rows.title: Music in the Air
rows.cast: Gloria Swanson, John Boles
rows.extract: Music in the Air is a 1934 American romantic comedy musical film based on Jerome Kern and Oscar Hammerstein II's Broadway musical of the same name. It was part of the popular subgenre of operetta films made during the era. The film was a commercial failure on its release, losing $389,000. This was t

rows.title: The Mysterious Mr. Wong
rows.cast: Bela Lugosi, Arline Judge, Wallace Ford
rows.extract: The Mysterious Mr. Wong is a tongue-in-cheek 1934 mystery film starring Bela Lugosi as a powerful Fu Manchu type criminal mastermind of the Chinatown underworld, and Wallace Ford as a wisecracking reporter. The film is based on Harry Stephen Keeler's 1928 short story "The Strange Adventure of the Tw

rows.title: The Mystery of Mr. X
rows.cast: Robert Montgomery, Elizabeth Allan
rows.extract: The Mystery of Mr. X is a 1934 American pre-Code crime film starring Robert Montgomery as a jewel thief who gets mixed up in a series of murders in London. It is based on the 1933 novel X v. Rex by Philip MacDonald, was remade in 1952 as The Hour of 13.

rows.title: Mystery Liner
rows.cast: Noah Beery, Astrid Allwyn
rows.extract: Mystery Liner is a 1934 American Pre-Code film directed by William Nigh, starring Noah Beery, Sr., and based on an Edgar Wallace story originally published in the Saturday Evening Post in 1924. The film was entered as a feature attraction at the 1934 International Exhibition of Cinematographic Art i

rows.title: Mystery Ranch
rows.cast: Tom Tyler, Roberta Gale
rows.extract: Mystery Ranch is a 1934 American comedy Western film co-produced and directed by Bernard B. Ray and starring Tom Tyler, Roberta Gale and Jack Perrin. It was Tyler's first of 18 films for Reliable Pictures.

rows.title: Name the Woman
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, Arline Judge
rows.extract: Name the Woman is a 1934 American mystery drama film directed by Albert S. Rogell and starring Richard Cromwell, Arline Judge and Rita La Roy. It is not a remake of the studio's 1928 silent film of the same name, although Variety wrongly reported this at the time.

rows.title: Nana
rows.cast: Anna Sten, Lionel Atwill
rows.extract: Nana is a 1934 American pre-Code film, produced by Samuel Goldwyn, released through United Artists, starring Anna Sten. and directed by Dorothy Arzner and George Fitzmaurice.

rows.title: Neath the Arizona Skies
rows.cast: John Wayne, Sheila Terry
rows.extract: 'Neath the Arizona Skies is a 1934 Western film directed by Harry L. Fraser, produced by Lone Star Productions, released by Monogram Pictures and starring John Wayne. Wayne's character attempts to locate a little girl's father, so that she may claim a $50,000 Indian oil claim. The film co-stars Shei

rows.title: The Ninth Guest
rows.cast: Genevieve Tobin, Donald Cook
rows.extract: The Ninth Guest, sometimes abbreviated as The 9th Guest, is a 1934 American pre-Code murder mystery film directed by Roy William Neill and starring Donald Cook and Genevieve Tobin.

rows.title: No Greater Glory
rows.cast: George P. Breakston, Jimmy Butler
rows.extract: No Greater Glory is a 1934 American Pre-Code allegorical anti-war film directed by Frank Borzage and based on the novel A Pál utcai fiúk by Ferenc Molnár, known in English as "The Boys of Paul Street." The film's box office performance was described as "dismal".

rows.title: No More Women
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Victor McLaglen, Sally Blane
rows.extract: No More Women is a 1934 American pre-Code adventure film directed by Albert S. Rogell and starring Edmund Lowe, Victor McLaglen, Sally Blane and Minna Gombell. The film was released and distributed by Paramount Pictures. It was part of a long-running series that paired Lowe and McLaglen as friendly

rows.title: No Ransom
rows.cast: Leila Hyams, Phillips Holmes, Jack La Rue
rows.extract: No Ransom is a 1934 American film directed by Frec C. Newmeyer.

rows.title: The Notorious Sophie Lang
rows.cast: Gertrude Michael, Paul Cavanagh
rows.extract: The Notorious Sophie Lang is a 1934 American crime drama film directed by Ralph Murphy and starring Gertrude Michael, Paul Cavanagh and Alison Skipworth.

rows.title: Now and Forever
rows.cast: Gary Cooper, Carole Lombard, Shirley Temple
rows.extract: Now and Forever is a 1934 American drama film directed by Henry Hathaway. The screenplay by Vincent Lawrence and Sylvia Thalberg was based on the story "Honor Bright" by Jack Kirkland and Melville Baker. The film stars Gary Cooper, Carole Lombard, and Shirley Temple in a story about a small-time swi

rows.title: Now I'll Tell
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Helen Twelvetrees, Alice Faye
rows.extract: Now I'll Tell is a 1934 American Pre-Code drama film directed by Edwin J. Burke starring Spencer Tracy, Helen Twelvetrees, and Alice Faye. It was produced by Fox Film shortly before the company's merger with Twentieth Century Pictures. It marked the final screen appearance of former silent star Alic

rows.title: Of Human Bondage
rows.cast: Bette Davis, Leslie Howard, Kay Johnson
rows.extract: Of Human Bondage is a 1934 American drama film directed by John Cromwell and regarded by critics as the film that made Bette Davis a star. The screenplay by Lester Cohen is based on the 1915 novel Of Human Bondage by W. Somerset Maugham.

rows.title: The Oil Raider
rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Gloria Shea, George Irving
rows.extract: The Oil Raider is a 1934 American action film directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet and starring Buster Crabbe, Gloria Shea and George Irving. It was produced on Poverty Row as a second feature and was distributed by independent company Mayfair Pictures.

rows.title: The Old Fashioned Way
rows.cast: W. C. Fields, Baby LeRoy, Judith Allen
rows.extract: The Old Fashioned Way is a 1934 American comedy film produced by Paramount Pictures. The film was directed by William Beaudine and stars W. C. Fields. The script was written by Jack Cunningham based on a story by "Charles Bogle".

rows.title: Once to Every Bachelor
rows.cast: Marian Nixon, Neil Hamilton
rows.extract: Once to Every Bachelor is a 1934 American drama film directed by William Nigh and starring Marian Nixon, Neil Hamilton and William Austin.

rows.title: Once to Every Woman
rows.cast: Ralph Bellamy, Fay Wray
rows.extract: Once to Every Woman is a 1934 American pre-Code film adaptation of A. J. Cronin's 1933 short story Kaleidoscope in "K". The film was made by Columbia Pictures and stars Ralph Bellamy and Fay Wray.

rows.title: One Exciting Adventure
rows.cast: Binnie Barnes, Neil Hamilton, Paul Cavanagh
rows.extract: One Exciting Adventure is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Ernst L. Frank and starring Binnie Barnes, Neil Hamilton and Paul Cavanagh. It is a remake of the 1933 German film What Women Dream.

rows.title: One Hour Late
rows.cast: Helen Twelvetrees, Conrad Nagel
rows.extract: One Hour Late is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Ralph Murphy and written by Kathryn Scola and Paul Gerard Smith. rows.title: One in a Million
rows.cast: Dorothy Wilson, Charles Starrett
rows.extract: One in a Million is a 1934 American drama film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring Dorothy Wilson, Charles Starrett and Guinn 'Big Boy' Williams.

rows.title: One Is Guilty
rows.cast: Ralph Bellamy, Shirley Grey
rows.extract: One Is Guilty is a 1934 American pre-Code mystery crime film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Ralph Bellamy, Shirley Grey and Rita La Roy. rows.title: One More River
rows.cast: Diana Wynyard, Frank Lawton, Jane Wyatt
rows.extract: One More River is a 1934 American drama film mystery directed by James Whale. It was produced and distributed by Universal Pictures and starred Colin Clive, Diana Wynyard and stage actress Mrs Patrick Campbell in one of her very few films. The film marked Jane Wyatt's screen debut. It is based on th

rows.title: One Night of Love
rows.cast: Grace Moore, Mona Barrie, Tullio Carminati
rows.extract: One Night of Love is a 1934 American Columbia Pictures romantic musical film set in the opera world, starring Grace Moore and Tullio Carminati. The film was directed by Victor Schertzinger and adapted from the story Don't Fall in Love, by Charles Beahan and Dorothy Speare.

rows.title: Operator 13
rows.cast: Marion Davies, Gary Cooper, The Mills Brothers
rows.extract: Operator 13 is a 1934 American pre-Code romance film directed by Richard Boleslawski and starring Marion Davies, Gary Cooper, and Jean Parker.

rows.title: Orient Express
rows.cast: Heather Angel, Ralph Morgan
rows.extract: Orient Express is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Paul Martin and starring Heather Angel, Norman Foster and Ralph Morgan. It is based on the 1932 novel Stamboul Train by Graham Greene.

rows.title: Our Daily Bread
rows.cast: Karen Morley, Tom Keene, Barbara Pepper
rows.extract: Our Daily Bread is a 1934 American drama film directed by King Vidor and starring Karen Morley, Tom Keene, and John Qualen. rows.title: Outcast Lady
rows.cast: Constance Bennett, Herbert Marshall, Hugh Williams
rows.extract: Outcast Lady is a 1934 sound film directed by Robert Z. Leonard and produced and distributed by Metro Goldwyn Mayer. rows.cast: Jimmy Durante, Lupe Vélez, Stuart Erwin
rows.extract: Palooka is a 1934 American Pre-Code comedy film directed by Benjamin Stoloff and starring Stuart Erwin in the titular role, Lupe Velez and Jimmy Durante, and based on the comic strip by Ham Fisher. rows.title: Paradise Valley
rows.cast: Wheeler Oakman, Walter Brennan
rows.extract: Paradise Valley is a 1934 American western film directed by James P. Hogan and starring Jean Chatburn, Wheeler Oakman and Walter Brennan. It was an independent production made on Poverty Row.

rows.title: Pardon My Pups
rows.cast: Junior Coghlan, Shirley Temple
rows.extract: Pardon My Pups is a 1934 Shirley Temple short film about a young boy named Sonny Rogers who wants a motorcycle for his birthday but his stubborn father insists on getting an expensive hunting dog instead even though Sonny hates dogs and the father blatantly just wants the dog for himself. Sonny runs

rows.title: Paris Interlude
rows.cast: Madge Evans, Robert Young, Ted Healy
rows.extract: Paris Interlude is a 1934 American drama film directed by Edwin L. Marin and written by Wells Root. The film stars Madge Evans, Otto Kruger, Robert Young, Una Merkel, Ted Healy and Louise Henry. The film was released on July 27, 1934, by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: The Party's Over
rows.cast: Stuart Erwin, Ann Sothern
rows.extract: The Party's Over is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Walter Lang.

rows.title: Peck's Bad Boy
rows.cast: Jackie Cooper, Thomas Meighan, Dorothy Peterson
rows.extract: Henry "Hennery" Peck, popularly known as Peck's Bad Boy, is a fictional character created by George Wilbur Peck (1840–1916). rows.cast: George J. Lewis, Dorothy Gulliver
rows.extract: The Pecos Dandy is a 1934 American western film directed by Victor Adamson and Horace B. Carpenter and starring George J. Lewis, Dorothy Gulliver and Robert Walker. It was produced on Poverty Row as a second feature. It is now considered a lost film.

rows.title: The Personality Kid
rows.cast: Pat O'Brien, Glenda Farrell, Claire Dodd
rows.extract: The Personality Kid is a 1934 American drama film directed by Alan Crosland, starring Pat O'Brien and Glenda Farrell. The film was based on a story by Gene Towne and C. Graham Baker. It was released by Warner Bros. on July 7, 1934. A young prizefighter's success corrupts him and leads him to neglect

rows.title: The Poor Rich
rows.cast: Edward Everett Horton, Edna May Oliver
rows.extract: The Poor Rich is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by Edward Sedgwick and written by Ebba Havez and Dale Van Every. rows.title: Port of Lost Dreams
rows.cast: William Boyd, George F. Marion, Lola Lane
rows.extract: Port of Lost Dreams is a 1934 American drama film directed by Frank R. Strayer and starring William Boyd, Lola Lane and George F. Marion.

rows.title: The Prescott Kid
rows.cast: Tim McCoy, Sheila Mannors
rows.extract: The Prescott Kid is a 1934 American Western film directed by David Selman, from an original screenplay by Ford Beebe, which stars Tim McCoy, Sheila Mannors, and Joseph Sauers. rows.title: The President Vanishes
rows.cast: Edward Arnold, Arthur Byron
rows.extract: The President Vanishes is a 1934 American political drama film directed by William A. Wellman and produced by Walter Wanger. Starring Edward Arnold and Arthur Byron, the film is an adaptation of Rex Stout's political novel of the same name.

rows.title: The Private Life of Don Juan
rows.cast: Douglas Fairbanks, Merle Oberon, Benita Hume
rows.extract: The Private Life of Don Juan is a 1934 British comedy-drama film directed by Alexander Korda and starring Douglas Fairbanks, Merle Oberon and Benita Hume. rows.title: Private Scandal
rows.cast: ZaSu Pitts, Phillips Holmes
rows.extract: Private Scandal is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by Ralph Murphy and written by Vera Caspary, Garrett Fort and Bruce Manning. rows.cast: Rosemary Ames, Victor Jory
rows.extract: Pursued is a 1934 American drama film directed by Louis King and starring Rosemary Ames, Victor Jory and Russell Hardie. Produced and distributed by Fox Film Corporation. rows.title: The Quitter

rows.extract: The Quitter is a 1934 American drama film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Charley Grapewin, Emma Dunn and Barbara Weeks. It was produced and distributed by the Poverty Row studio Chesterfield Pictures, later absorbed into Republic.

rows.title: Randy Rides Alone
rows.cast: John Wayne, Alberta Vaughn
rows.extract: Randy Rides Alone is a 1934 American Pre-Code Western film starring John Wayne, Yakima Canutt, and George Hayes. The 53-minute black-and-white film was directed by Harry L. Fraser, produced by Paul Malvern for Lone Star Productions, and released by Monogram Pictures.

rows.title: Red Morning
rows.cast: Steffi Duna, Regis Toomey
rows.extract: Red Morning is a 1934 American adventure film directed by Wallace Fox from a screenplay by John Twist and Wallace Fox, based on a story by Gouverneur Morris. The film stars Steffi Duna, Regis Toomey, Raymond Hatton, and Mitchell Lewis.

rows.title: Registered Nurse
rows.cast: Bebe Daniels, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Registered Nurse is a 1934 American Pre-Code film produced by First National Pictures and released through its parent company Warner Bros. The film was directed by Robert Florey and stars Bebe Daniels in her final role for Warner Bros.

rows.title: Return of the Terror
rows.cast: Mary Astor, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Return of the Terror is a 1934 American mystery film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Peter Milne and Eugene Solow. rows.cast: Miriam Hopkins, Fay Wray, Joel McCrea
rows.extract: The Richest Girl in the World is a 1934 romantic comedy film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Miriam Hopkins and Joel McCrea. Norman Krasna was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Story. It was remade in 1944 as Bride by Mistake with Laraine Day and Alan Marshal.

rows.title: Riding Speed

rows.cast: Tom Tyler, Ruth Hiatt, Lafe McKee
rows.extract: Ridin' Thru is a 1934 American Western film directed by Harry S. Webb and starring Tom Tyler, Ruth Hiatt and Lafe McKee.

rows.title: Riptide
rows.cast: Norma Shearer, Robert Montgomery, Herbert Marshall
rows.extract: Riptide is a 1934 American pre-Code romantic drama film starring Norma Shearer, Robert Montgomery and Herbert Marshall, written and directed by Edmund Goulding, and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: The Road to Ruin
rows.cast: Helen Foster, Nell O'Day
rows.extract: The Road to Ruin is a 1934 pre-Code exploitation film directed by Dorothy Davenport, under the name "Mrs. Wallace Reid", and Melville Shyer, and written by Davenport with the uncredited contribution of the film's producer, Willis Kent. The film, now in the public domain, portrays a young woman whose

rows.title: Rocky Rhodes
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Sheila Terry
rows.extract: Rocky Rhodes is a 1934 American Western film directed by Alfred Raboch and written by Edward Churchill. The film stars Buck Jones, Sheila Terry, Stanley Fields, Walter Miller, Alfred P. James and Paul Fix. The film was released on September 24, 1934, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Romance in the Rain
rows.cast: Heather Angel, Esther Ralston
rows.extract: Romance in the Rain is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Stuart Walker and written by Barry Trivers and Gladys Buchanan Unger. rows.title: The Scarlet Empress
rows.cast: Marlene Dietrich, John Lodge, Sam Jaffe
rows.extract: The Scarlet Empress is a 1934 American historical drama film starring Marlene Dietrich and John Lodge about the life of Catherine the Great. It was directed and produced by Josef von Sternberg from a screenplay by Eleanor McGeary, loosely based on the diary of Catherine arranged by Manuel Komroff.

rows.title: The Scarlet Letter
rows.cast: Colleen Moore, Henry B. Walthall, Alan Hale
rows.extract: The Scarlet Letter is a 1934 American film directed by Robert G. Vignola and based on the 1850 novel of the same name by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

rows.cast: Sidney Fox, Lois Wilson
rows.extract: School for Girls is a 1935 American drama film directed by William Nigh and starring Sidney Fox, Paul Kelly and Lois Wilson.

rows.cast: Lon Chaney Jr., Sheila Terry

rows.cast: Buster Crabbe, Ida Lupino

rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Warren William, Glenda Farrell

rows.title: The Show-Off
rows.cast: Spencer Tracy, Madge Evans, Henry Wadsworth
rows.extract: The Show-Off is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Charles Reisner and starring Spencer Tracy, Madge Evans and Henry Wadsworth. It is notable for being the first movie Tracy made for Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer; he was on loan-out from Fox at the time and later moved to MGM.

rows.title: Side Streets
rows.cast: Aline MacMahon, Ann Dvorak, Paul Kelly
rows.extract: Side Streets, also known in the UK as A Woman in Her Thirties, is a 1934 American romantic melodrama film starring Aline MacMahon and Paul Kelly. The screenplay concerns a spinster who hires, then marries, a destitute sailor who is not always faithful.

rows.title: The Silver Streak
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Sally Blane
rows.extract: The Silver Streak is a 1934 American black-and-white film drama from RKO, loosely based on the record-setting "dawn-to-dusk" run of the Pioneer Zephyr on May 26, 1934. The film stars Sally Blane, Charles Starrett, William Farnum, and Hardie Albright.

rows.title: Sing and Like It
rows.cast: ZaSu Pitts, Pert Kelton, Edward Everett Horton

rows.title: Ticket to a Crime
rows.cast: Ralph Graves, Lois Wilson, Lola Lane
rows.extract: Ticket to a Crime is a 1934 American mystery film directed by Lewis D. Collins and starring Ralph Graves, Lois Wilson and Lola Lane. A private detective and his assistant solve a murder at a country club.

rows.title: Tomorrow's Youth
rows.cast: Dickie Moore, Gloria Shea
rows.extract: Tomorrow's Youth is a 1934 American film directed by Charles Lamont.

rows.title: The Trail Beyond
rows.cast: John Wayne, Verna Hillie, Noah Beery Sr.
rows.extract: The Trail Beyond is a 1934 Western film directed by Robert N. Bradbury and starring John Wayne, Noah Beery Sr., and Noah Beery Jr. The motion picture was based on the novel The Wolf Hunters by James Oliver Curwood, which was also adapted as a silent film (1926) and a later sound film (1949), both ca

rows.title: Transatlantic Merry-Go-Round
rows.cast: Jack Benny, Nancy Carroll, Sydney Howard
rows.extract: Transatlantic Merry-Go-Round is a 1934 American drama film with musical and comedic elements, directed by Benjamin Stoloff.

rows.title: Treasure Island
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Jackie Cooper, Lionel Barrymore
rows.extract: Treasure Island is a 1934 film directed by Victor Fleming and starring Wallace Beery, Jackie Cooper, Lionel Barrymore, Lewis Stone, and Nigel Bruce. It is an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's famous 1883 novel of the same name. Jim Hawkins discovers a treasure map and travels on a sailing ship

rows.title: The Trumpet Blows
rows.cast: George Raft, Adolphe Menjou, Frances Drake
rows.extract: The Trumpet Blows is a 1934 American Pre-Code film directed by Stephen Roberts, featuring George Raft as a Mexican matador, Adolphe Menjou as a retired bandito clearly based on Pancho Villa, and Frances Drake as Chulita, the woman they both want to marry.

rows.title: Twentieth Century
rows.cast: Carole Lombard, John Barrymore, Walter Connolly
rows.extract: Twentieth Century is a 1934 American pre-Code screwball comedy film directed by Howard Hawks and starring John Barrymore and Carole Lombard. Much of the film is set on the 20th Century Limited train as it travels from Chicago to New York City. Ben Hecht and Charles MacArthur adapted their 1932 Broad

rows.title: Twenty Million Sweethearts
rows.cast: Ginger Rogers, Dick Powell, Ted Fio Rito
rows.extract: Twenty Million Sweethearts is a 1934 American Pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Ray Enright and starring Pat O'Brien, Dick Powell, Ginger Rogers, and The Mills Brothers. The film was remade in 1949 as My Dream Is Yours.

rows.title: Twisted Rails
rows.cast: Philo McCullough, Donald Keith
rows.extract: Twisted Rails is a 1934 American Western film directed by Albert Herman. It was distributed by the independent Imperial Distributing Corporation for the states-rights market. The plot concerns $50,000 in gold that is hidden on a train and a gang's efforts to get it.

rows.title: Two Alone
rows.cast: Tom Brown, Jean Parker
rows.extract: Two Alone is a 1934 American Pre-Code film directed by Elliott Nugent and starring Tom Brown and Jean Parker. According to RKO records the film lost $158,000. Based on the play Wild Birds by Dan Totheroh, most remember the film primarily for its early skinny-dipping scene. Jean Parker was borrowed f

rows.title: Two Heads on a Pillow
rows.cast: Neil Hamilton, Miriam Jordan
rows.extract: Two Heads on a Pillow is a 1934 American romance film directed by William Nigh and written by Albert DeMond. The film stars Neil Hamilton, Miriam Jordan, Henry Armetta, Hardie Albright, Dorothy Appleby and Mary Forbes. The film was released on October 2, 1934, by Liberty Pictures.

rows.title: Uncertain Lady
rows.cast: Genevieve Tobin, Edward Everett Horton, Paul Cavanagh
rows.extract: Uncertain Lady is a 1934 American comedy film directed by Karl Freund, written by Daniel Evans, Doris Anderson, Edward A. Curtiss, George O'Neil and Don Ryan, and starring Edward Everett Horton, Genevieve Tobin, Paul Cavanagh, Mary Nash, Renee Gadd and Donald Reed. It was released on April 3, 1934,

rows.title: Unknown Blonde
rows.cast: Edward Arnold, Barbara Barondess, Dorothy Revier
rows.extract: Unknown Blonde is a 1934 American pre-Code crime drama film directed by Hobart Henley and starring Edward Arnold, Barbara Barondess and Dorothy Revier. It was released by the independent Majestic Pictures. It was based on the 1932 novel Collusion by Theodore D. Irwin. The film's sets were designed b

rows.title: Upper World
rows.cast: Ginger Rogers, Warren William, Mary Astor
rows.extract: Upperworld is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Roy Del Ruth and starring Warren William as a wealthy married railroad tycoon whose friendship with a showgirl, played by Ginger Rogers, leads to blackmail and murder. Upperworld is one of the last films released before the strict enforce

rows.title: A Very Honorable Guy
rows.cast: Joe E. Brown, Alice White, Irene Franklin
rows.extract: A Very Honorable Guy is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by Lloyd Bacon, written by Earl Baldwin, and starring Joe E. Brown, Alice White, Robert Barrat, Alan Dinehart, Irene Franklin and Hobart Cavanaugh. It was released by Warner Bros. on May 5, 1934.

rows.title: Viva Villa!
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Leo Carrillo, Mary Astor
rows.extract: Viva Villa! is a 1934 American pre-Code film directed by Jack Conway and starring Wallace Beery as Mexican revolutionary Pancho Villa. The screenplay was written by Ben Hecht, adapted from the 1933 book Viva Villa! by Edgecumb Pinchon and O. B. Stade. The film was shot on location in Mexico and prod

rows.title: Voice in the Night
rows.cast: Tim McCoy, Billie Seward, Ward Bond
rows.extract: Voice in the Night  is a 1934 American action film directed by Charles C. Coleman and starring Tim McCoy, Billie Seward, and Joseph Crehan. It was produced as a second feature by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Wagon Wheels
rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Gail Patrick
rows.extract: Wagon Wheels is a 1934 Western film directed by Charles Barton and starring Randolph Scott and Gail Patrick. It is a remake of 1931's Fighting Caravans, using stock footage from the original and substituting a new cast. It was based on the Zane Grey novel Fighting Caravans. The supporting cast featu

rows.title: Wake Up and Dream
rows.cast: Russ Columbo, June Knight
rows.extract: Wake Up and Dream is a 1934 American musical film directed by Kurt Neumann, written by John Meehan Jr., and starring Russ Columbo, Roger Pryor, June Knight, Catherine Doucet, Henry Armetta and Andy Devine. It was released on October 1, 1934, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: The Way of the West
rows.cast: Hal Taliaferro, William Desmond
rows.extract: The Way of the West is a 1934 American Western film directed by Robert Emmett Tansey.

rows.title: We Live Again
rows.cast: Anna Sten, Fredric March, C. Aubrey Smith
rows.extract: We Live Again is a 1934 film directed by Rouben Mamoulian and starring Anna Sten and Fredric March. The film is an adaptation of Leo Tolstoy's 1899 novel Resurrection (Voskraeseniye). The screenplay was written by Maxwell Anderson with contributions from a number of writers, including Preston Sturge

rows.title: We're Not Dressing
rows.cast: Bing Crosby, George Burns, Gracie Allen
rows.extract: We're Not Dressing is a 1934 pre-Code screwball musical comedy film directed by Norman Taurog and starring Bing Crosby, Carole Lombard, George Burns, Gracie Allen and Ethel Merman. Based on the 1902 J. M. Barrie play The Admirable Crichton, the film is about a beautiful yacht owner (Lombard) who bec

rows.title: We're Rich Again
rows.cast: Billie Burke, Edna May Oliver, Buster Crabbe
rows.extract: We're Rich Again is a 1934 American comedy-drama film directed by William A. Seiter and starring Edna May Oliver, Billie Burke, and Marian Nixon. It is based on the play And Who Will Be Clever by Alden Nash.

rows.title: Wednesday's Child
rows.cast: Karen Morley, Edward Arnold, Frankie Thomas
rows.extract: Wednesday's Child is a 1934 American drama film directed by John S. Robertson and written by Willis Goldbeck, based on the 1934 play Wednesday's Child by Leopold L. Atlas. The film stars Karen Morley, Edward Arnold, Frankie Thomas, Robert Shayne and Frank Conroy. The film was released on October 26,

rows.title: West of the Divide
rows.cast: John Wayne, Virginia Faire Brown, George Hayes
rows.extract: West of the Divide is a 1934 American Western film directed by Robert N. Bradbury for Monogram, and starring John Wayne, Yakima Canutt and Gabby Hayes.

rows.title: West of the Pecos
rows.cast: Richard Dix, Samuel S. Hinds, Martha Sleeper
rows.extract: West of the Pecos is a 1934 American Western film directed by Phil Rosen and starring Richard Dix and Martha Sleeper. The screenplay was written Milton Krims and John Twist, who adapted the serial of the same name by Zane Grey, appearing beginning in The American Magazine in 1931 and later as the 19

rows.title: Western Racketeers
rows.cast: Bill Cody, Edna Aslin, Hal Taliaferro
rows.extract: Western Racketeers is a 1934 American western film directed by Robert J. Horner and starring Bill Cody, Edna Aslin and Hal Taliaferro It was an independent film produced on Poverty Row.

rows.title: The Westerner
rows.cast: Tim McCoy, Marion Shilling
rows.extract: The Westerner is a 1934 American Western film directed by David Selman and starring Tim McCoy, Marion Shilling and Joe Sawyer. It was released by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Wharf Angel
rows.cast: Victor McLaglen, Dorothy Dell
rows.extract: Wharf Angel is a 1934 American drama film directed by William Cameron Menzies and George Somnes and starring Victor McLaglen, Dorothy Dell, David Landau, and Preston Foster. Wharf Angel was the first screenplay of Stephen Morehouse Avery.

rows.title: What Every Woman Knows
rows.cast: Helen Hayes, Madge Evans, Dudley Digges
rows.extract: What Every Woman Knows is a 1934 American romantic comedy film directed by Gregory La Cava and starring Helen Hayes, Brian Aherne and Madge Evans. The film was produced and distributed by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and is based on the play What Every Woman Knows (1908) by J. M. Barrie. It was filmed by Par

rows.title: What's Your Racket?
rows.cast: Regis Toomey, Noel Francis, J. Carrol Naish
rows.extract: What's Your Racket? is a 1934 American Pre-Code crime film directed by Fred Guiol and starring Regis Toomey, Noel Francis and J. Carrol Naish. It was produced on Poverty Row by independent studio Mayfair Pictures.

rows.title: When a Man Sees Red
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Dorothy Revier
rows.extract: When a Man Sees Red is a 1934 American Western film written and directed by Alan James and starring Buck Jones, Peggy Campbell, Dorothy Revier, LeRoy Mason, Syd Saylor and Frank LaRue. It was released on November 24, 1934, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: When Lightning Strikes
rows.cast: Francis X. Bushman Jr., Tom London
rows.extract: For the Kiss song see Sonic Boom

rows.title: When Strangers Meet
rows.cast: Richard Cromwell, Arline Judge
rows.extract: When Strangers Meet is a 1934 American drama film directed by Christy Cabanne and starring Richard Cromwell, Arline Judge, and Lucien Littlefield. It was released on July 20, 1934.

rows.title: Whirlpool
rows.cast: Jean Arthur, Jack Holt, Donald Cook
rows.extract: Whirlpool is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Roy William Neill and starring Jack Holt and Jean Arthur. The screenplay concerns a carnival owner convicted of manslaughter after a man is killed in a fight.

rows.title: The Whirlwind Rider
rows.cast: Jay Wilsey, George Chesebro

rows.title: The White Parade
rows.cast: Loretta Young, John Boles, Dorothy Wilson
rows.extract: The White Parade is a 1934 film directed by Irving Cummings and starring Loretta Young and John Boles. It was written by Rian James, Jesse Lasky Jr., Sonya Levien and Ernest Pascal, from the novel by Rian James.

rows.title: Whom the Gods Destroy
rows.cast: Walter Connolly, Robert Young, Doris Kenyon
rows.extract: Whom the Gods Destroy is a 1934 American drama film directed by Walter Lang and starring Walter Connolly.

rows.title: A Wicked Woman
rows.cast: Mady Christians, Jean Parker, Charles Bickford
rows.extract: A Wicked Woman is a 1934 drama film directed by Charles Brabin and starring Mady Christians as a woman who kills her abusive husband to protect her family and builds a new life to raise their four children. The film also stars Jean Parker and Charles Bickford. It was based on the novel Wicked Woman

rows.title: Wild Cargo
rows.cast: Frank Buck
rows.extract: Wild Cargo is a 1934 jungle adventure documentary starring Frank Buck. Buck depicts the ingenious methods by which he traps wild birds, mammals and reptiles. Many scenes were photographed on the vast Malayan estates of Buck's friend, Sultan Ibrahim of Johor, who appears in person in the film.

rows.title: Wild Gold
rows.cast: John Boles, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: Wild Gold is a 1934 American romance film directed by George Marshall and written by Lester Cole and Henry Johnson. The film stars John Boles, Claire Trevor, Harry Green, Roger Imhof, Ruth Gillette, Monroe Owsley and Edward Gargan. The film was released on June 8, 1934, by Fox Film Corporation.

rows.title: The Witching Hour
rows.cast: John Halliday, Judith Allen, William Frawley
rows.extract: The Witching Hour is a 1934 American pre-Code drama film directed by Henry Hathaway and starring Sir Guy Standing, John Halliday, Judith Allen and Tom Brown.

rows.title: The Woman Condemned
rows.cast: Claudia Dell, Lola Lane, Jason Robards Sr.
rows.extract: The Woman Condemned is a 1934 American pre-Code film directed by Dorothy Davenport, best known as a silent actress and the wife of actor Wallace Reid.

rows.title: Woman in the Dark
rows.cast: Fay Wray, Ralph Bellamy, Melvyn Douglas
rows.extract: Woman in the Dark is a 1934 American crime drama film directed by Phil Rosen and based on a 1933 short story by Dashiell Hammett. It was filmed at Biograph Studios by Select Pictures and released by RKO Radio Pictures.

rows.title: A Woman's Man
rows.cast: John Halliday, Marguerite De La Motte
rows.extract: A Woman's Man is a 1934 American pre-Code comedy film directed by Edward Ludwig and starring John Halliday, Marguerite De La Motte and Wallace Ford. The screenplay concerns a film star diva who storms off the film set and begins a romance with a publicity-hungry boxer.

rows.title: Wonder Bar
rows.cast: Al Jolson, Dolores del Río, Kay Francis
rows.extract: Wonder Bar is a 1934 American pre-Code film adaptation of a Broadway musical of the same name directed by Lloyd Bacon with musical numbers created by Busby Berkeley.

rows.title: The World Accuses
rows.cast: Dickie Moore, Cora Sue Collins
rows.extract: The World Accuses is a 1934 American drama film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Vivian Tobin, Dickie Moore and Cora Sue Collins.

rows.title: The World Moves On
rows.cast: Franchot Tone, Madeleine Carroll, Reginald Denny
rows.extract: The World Moves On is a 1934 American drama film directed by John Ford and starring Madeleine Carroll and Franchot Tone. It was the first Hollywood code approved film.

rows.title: You Belong to Me
rows.cast: Lee Tracy, Helen Mack, Helen Morgan
rows.extract: You Belong to Me is a 1934 American drama film directed by Alfred L. Werker and written by Elizabeth Alexander, Walter DeLeon, Grover Jones and William Slavens McNutt. The film stars Lee Tracy, Helen Mack, Helen Morgan, David Holt, Arthur Pierson, Lynne Overman and Dean Jagger. The film was released

rows.title: You Can't Buy Everything
rows.cast: May Robson, Jean Parker, Lewis Stone
rows.extract: You Can't Buy Everything is a 1934 American pre-Code romantic drama film directed by Charles Reisner and Sandy Roth and starring May Robson, Jean Parker and Lewis Stone. It was released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. Working titles of the film were Rich Widow and Old Hannibal. According to Motion Picture H

rows.title: You're Telling Me!
rows.cast: W. C. Fields, Buster Crabbe, Joan Marsh
rows.extract: You're Telling Me! is a 1934 pre-Code comedy film directed by Erle C. Kenton and starring W.C. Fields. It is a remake of the silent film So's Your Old Man (1926), also starring Fields. Both films are adapted from the story Mr. Bisbee’s Princess by Julian Leonard Street. It was released by Paramount

rows.title: Young and Beautiful
rows.cast: William Haines, Joseph Cawthorn, Judith Allen
rows.extract: Young and Beautiful is a 1934 American romantic comedy film directed by Joseph Santley and starring William Haines and Judith Allen. The screenplay concerns a press agent who goes to great lengths to make his actress girlfriend a star, only to risk losing her in the process.

rows.title: $10 Raise
rows.cast: Edward Everett Horton, Karen Morley
rows.extract: $10 Raise is a 1935 American comedy film directed by George Marshall, written by Henry Johnson and Lou Breslow, and starring Edward Everett Horton, Karen Morley, Alan Dinehart, Glen Boles, Berton Churchill and Rosina Lawrence. It was released on May 4, 1935, by Fox Film Corporation.

rows.title: 1,000 Dollars a Minute
rows.cast: Leila Hyams, Edward Brophy
rows.extract: 1,000 Dollars a Minute is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Aubrey Scotto and starring Roger Pryor and Leila Hyams. The film was released on October 22, 1935. The film was nominated for an Academy Award in the category Sound Recording.

rows.title: Accent on Youth
rows.cast: Sylvia Sidney, Herbert Marshall
rows.extract: Accent on Youth is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Wesley Ruggles and written by Herbert Fields and Claude Binyon based on the 1934 play of the same name written by Samson Raphaelson. The film stars Sylvia Sidney and Herbert Marshall and features Phillip Reed, Holmes Herbert, Catherine Douce

rows.title: Adventurous Knights
rows.cast: David Sharpe, Gertrude Messinger, Mary Kornman

rows.title: The Affair of Susan
rows.cast: ZaSu Pitts, Hugh O'Connell
rows.extract: The Affair of Susan is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Kurt Neumann and starring Zasu Pitts, Hugh O'Connell and Walter Catlett. It is a remake of the 1928 silent film Lonesome. Two lonely people meet at an amusement park on Coney Island.

rows.title: After Office Hours
rows.cast: Constance Bennett, Clark Gable, Billie Burke
rows.extract: After Office Hours is a 1935 crime drama film directed by Robert Z. Leonard and starring Clark Gable and Constance Bennett. The screenplay was written by Herman Mankiewicz.

rows.title: After the Dance
rows.cast: Nancy Carroll, George Murphy, Thelma Todd
rows.extract: After the Dance is a 1935 American Proto-Noir, crime romance drama film melodrama directed by Leo Bulgakov and starring Nancy Carroll, George Murphy and Thelma Todd.

rows.title: Age of Indiscretion
rows.cast: Paul Lukas, Madge Evans, Helen Vinson
rows.extract: Age of Indiscretion is a 1935 American drama film directed by Edward Ludwig and written by Leon Gordon and Otis Garrett. The film stars Paul Lukas, Madge Evans, Helen Vinson, May Robson, David Holt and Ralph Forbes.

rows.title: Ah, Wilderness!
rows.cast: Wallace Beery, Lionel Barrymore, Mickey Rooney
rows.extract: Ah, Wilderness! is a 1935 American comedy-drama film adaptation of the 1933 Eugene O'Neill play of the same name. rows.cast: Ralph Bellamy, Tala Birell, Douglass Dumbrille
rows.extract: Air Hawks is a 1935 American aviation-themed science fiction film based on Ben Pivar's "Air Fury", an unpublished story. rows.title: Alias Mary Dow
rows.cast: Sally Eilers, Ray Milland
rows.extract: Alias Mary Dow is a 1935 American drama film directed by Kurt Neumann and starring Sally Eilers, Ray Milland and Henry O'Neill.

rows.title: Alibi Ike
rows.cast: Joe E. Brown, Olivia de Havilland
rows.extract: Alibi Ike is a 1935 American romantic comedy film directed by Ray Enright and starring Joe E. Brown, Olivia de Havilland and William Frawley. rows.cast: Katharine Hepburn, Fred MacMurray, Evelyn Venable
rows.extract: Alice Adams is a 1935 romantic drama film directed by George Stevens and starring Katharine Hepburn. It was made by RKO and produced by Pandro S. Berman. rows.extract: All the Kings Horses is a 1935 American comedy musical film adapted from the 1934 Broadway musical of the same name by Frederick Herendeen and Edward A. rows.title: Anna Karenina
rows.cast: Greta Garbo, Fredric March, Maureen O'Sullivan
rows.extract: Anna Karenina is a 1935 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer film adaptation of the 1877 novel Anna Karenina by Leo Tolstoy and directed by Clarence Brown. The film stars Greta Garbo, Fredric March, Basil Rathbone, and Maureen O'Sullivan. There are several other film adaptations of the novel.

rows.title: Annapolis Farewell
rows.cast: Guy Standing, Richard Cromwell
rows.extract: Annapolis Farewell is a 1935 American drama film directed by Alexander Hall and written by Frank Craven and Jack Wagner. The film stars Guy Standing, Rosalind Keith, Tom Brown, Richard Cromwell, John Howard and Benny Baker. The film was released on August 23, 1935, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Annie Oakley
rows.cast: Barbara Stanwyck, Melvyn Douglas, Preston Foster
rows.extract: Annie Oakley is a 1935 American Western film directed by George Stevens and starring Barbara Stanwyck, Preston Foster, Melvyn Douglas and Moroni Olsen. The film is based on the life of Annie Oakley.

rows.title: Another Face
rows.cast: Wallace Ford, Brian Donlevy, Phyllis Brooks
rows.extract: Another Face is a 1935 film directed by Christy Cabanne and starring Wallace Ford, Brian Donlevy and Phyllis Brooks. A wanted gangster has plastic surgery and becomes an actor.

rows.title: Arizona Bad Man
rows.cast: Reb Russell, Lois January, Edmund Cobb
rows.extract: Arizona Bad Man is a 1935 American Western film directed by S. Roy Luby and starring Reb Russell, Lois January and Edmund Cobb.

rows.title: The Arizonian
rows.cast: Richard Dix, Margot Grahame, Preston Foster, Louis Calhern
rows.extract: The Arizonian is a 1935 American Western film directed by Charles Vidor and starring Richard Dix, Margot Grahame, Preston Foster, and Louis Calhern. The screenplay was by Dudley Nichols. The film was released by RKO Radio Pictures on June 28, 1935.

rows.title: Atlantic Adventure
rows.cast: Nancy Carroll, Lloyd Nolan
rows.extract: Atlantic Adventure is a 1935 American comedy mystery film directed by Albert S. Rogell and starring Nancy Carroll, Lloyd Nolan and Harry Langdon.

rows.title: The Awakening of Jim Burke
rows.cast: Jack Holt, Florence Rice
rows.extract: The Awakening of Jim Burke is a 1935 American drama film directed by Lambert Hillyer and written by Michael L. Simmons. The film stars Jack Holt, Florence Rice, Jimmy Butler, Kathleen Burke, Robert Middlemass and Ralph Remley. The film was released on May 18, 1935, by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Baby Face Harrington
rows.cast: Charles Butterworth, Una Merkel, Nat Pendleton
rows.extract: Baby Face Harrington is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Raoul Walsh and written by Nunnally Johnson, Edwin H. Knopf and Charles Lederer. rows.title: Bad Boy
rows.cast: James Dunn, Dorothy Wilson
rows.extract: Bad Boy is a 1935 American comedy film directed by John G. Blystone and written by Allen Rivkin. The film stars James Dunn, Dorothy Wilson, Louise Fazenda, Victor Kilian, John Wray and Luis Alberni. The film was released on October 25, 1935, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: Bar 20 Rides Again
rows.cast: William Boyd, Jean Rouverol
rows.extract: Bar 20 Rides Again is a 1935 American Western film directed by Howard Bretherton and written by Gerald Geraghty and Doris Schroeder. The film stars William Boyd, James Ellison, Jean Rouverol, George "Gabby" Hayes, Harry Worth, Frank McGlynn Jr. and Howard Lang. The film was released on December 6, 1

rows.title: Barbary Coast
rows.cast: Edward G. Robinson, Miriam Hopkins, Joel McCrea
rows.extract: Barbary Coast is a 1935 American historical Western film directed by Howard Hawks. It features a wide range of actors, from hero Joel M

rows.title: Becky Sharp
rows.cast: Miriam Hopkins, Cedric Hardwicke, Frances Dee
rows.extract: Becky Sharp is a 1935 American Technicolor historical drama film directed by Rouben Mamoulian and starring Miriam Hopkins who was nominated for the Best Actress Oscar. rows.title: Behind the Evidence
rows.cast: Norman Foster, Sheila Bromley
rows.extract: Behind the Evidence is a 1935 American crime film directed by Lambert Hillyer and starring Norman Foster, Sheila Bromley and Donald Cook. It was produced and distributed by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Behind the Green Lights
rows.cast: Norman Foster, Judith Allen
rows.extract: Behind the Green Lights is a 1935 American crime film directed by Christy Cabanne and starring Norman Foster, Judith Allen and Sidney Blackmer.

rows.title: The Best Man Wins
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Jack Holt, Bela Lugosi
rows.extract: The Best Man Wins is a 1935 American crime film directed by Erle C. Kenton and starring Edmund Lowe, Jack Holt and Bela Lugosi.

rows.title: The Big Broadcast of 1936
rows.cast: George Burns, Gracie Allen, Ethel Merman
rows.extract: The Big Broadcast of 1936 is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Norman Taurog, and is the second in the series of Big Broadcast movies.

rows.title: Biography of a Bachelor Girl
rows.cast: Ann Harding, Robert Montgomery, Edward Arnold
rows.extract: Biography of a Bachelor Girl is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Edward H. Griffith and written by Horace Jackson and Anita Loos. It is based upon the play, "Biography," by S. N. rows.title: The Bishop Misbehaves
rows.cast: Edmund Gwenn, Maureen O'Sullivan
rows.extract: The Bishop Misbehaves is a 1935 American comedy crime film directed by E. A. Dupont and starring Edmund Gwenn, Maureen O'Sullivan and Lucile Watson. It was based on the 1934 play of the same title by Frederick J. Jackson. Dupont made the film after signing a one-film contract with Metro-Goldwyn-Maye

rows.title: Black Fury
rows.cast: Paul Muni, Karen Morley, Barton MacLane
rows.extract: Black Fury is a 1935 American crime film directed by Michael Curtiz and starring Paul Muni, Karen Morley, and William Gargan. It was adapted by Abem Finkel and Carl Erickson from the short story "Jan Volkanik" by Judge Michael A. Musmanno and the play Bohunk by Harry R. Irving. The plot is based on

rows.title: The Black Room
rows.cast: Boris Karloff
rows.extract: The Black Room is a 1935 American horror film directed by Roy William Neill and starring Boris Karloff. Cinematography was done by Allen G. Siegler.

rows.title: Black Sheep
rows.cast: Edmund Lowe, Claire Trevor
rows.extract: Black Sheep is a 1935 American drama film directed by Allan Dwan and starring Edmund Lowe, Claire Trevor, and Tom Brown.

rows.title: Bonnie Scotland
rows.cast: Stan Laurel, Oliver Hardy, June Lang
rows.extract: Bonnie Scotland is a 1935 American film directed by James W. Horne and starring Laurel and Hardy. It was produced by Hal Roach for Hal Roach Studios. Although the film begins in Scotland, a large part of the action is set in British India.

rows.title: Bordertown
rows.cast: Paul Muni, Bette Davis, Margaret Lindsay
rows.extract: Bordertown is a 1935 American drama film directed by Archie Mayo and starring Paul Muni and Bette Davis. The screenplay by Laird Doyle and Wallace Smith is based on Robert Lord's adaptation of the 1934 novel Border Town by Carroll Graham. The supporting cast features Margaret Lindsay, Eugene Pallett

rows.title: Border Brigands
rows.cast: Buck Jones, Lona Andre
rows.extract: Border Brigands is a 1935 American Western film directed by Nick Grinde and written by Stuart Anthony. The film stars Buck Jones, Lona Andre, Fred Kohler, Frank Rice, Hank Bell and Edward Keane. The film was released on June 1, 1935, by Universal Pictures.

rows.title: Born to Battle
rows.cast: Tom Tyler, Jean Carmen
rows.extract: Born to Battle is a 1935 American Western film produced by Bernard B. Ray and Harry S. Webb and directed by Webb for Reliable Pictures.

rows.title: Born to Gamble
rows.cast: Onslow Stevens, H. B. Warner, Maxine Doyle
rows.extract: Born to Gamble (1935) is an American film directed by Phil Rosen and released by Republic Pictures.

rows.title: Break of Hearts
rows.cast: Katharine Hepburn, Charles Boyer
rows.extract: Break of Hearts is a 1935 RKO film starring Katharine Hepburn and Charles Boyer. The screenplay was written by the team of Sarah Y. Mason and Victor Heerman, with Anthony Veiller, from a story by Lester Cohen, specifically for Hepburn.

rows.title: The Bride Comes Home
rows.cast: Claudette Colbert, Fred MacMurray, Robert Young
rows.extract: The Bride Comes Home is a 1935 comedy film made by Paramount Pictures, directed by Wesley Ruggles, and starring Claudette Colbert, Fred MacMurray and Robert Young. It was written by Claude Binyon and Elisabeth Sanxay Holding.

rows.title: Bride of Frankenstein
rows.cast: Boris Karloff, Elsa Lanchester, Colin Clive
rows.extract: Bride of Frankenstein is a 1935 American science fiction horror film, and the first sequel to Universal Pictures' 1931 film Frankenstein. rows.title: Bright Lights
rows.cast: Joe E. Brown, Ann Dvorak, Patricia Ellis

rows.cast: Winifred Shaw, Genevieve Tobin, Lyle Talbot
rows.extract: Broadway Hostess is a 1935 American romantic comedy musical film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Wini Shaw, Genevieve Tobin and Lyle Talbot. rows.title: Broadway Melody of 1936
rows.cast: Eleanor Powell, Robert Taylor, Jack Benny
rows.extract: Broadway Melody of 1936 is a musical film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer in 1935. In New York, the film opened at the Capitol Theatre, the site of many prestigious MGM premieres. It was a follow-up of sorts to the successful The Broadway Melody, which had been released in 1929, although, there is n

rows.cast: Clark Gable, Loretta Young, Jack Oakie
rows.extract: Call of the Wild is a 1935 American adventure western film an adaptation of Jack London's 1903 novel The Call of the Wild. The film is directed by William A. rows.cast: Jack La Rue, Lillian Miles
rows.extract: Calling All Cars is a 1935 American crime film directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet and starring Jack La Rue, Lillian Miles and Jack Norton. It was originally made for distribution by Mayfair Pictures, but the company had ceased business by the time of its release.

rows.title: The Calling of Dan Matthews
rows.cast: Richard Arlen, Charlotte Wynters, Donald Cook
rows.extract: The Calling of Dan Matthews is a 1935 American crime film directed by Phil Rosen and starring Richard Arlen, Charlotte Wynters and Douglass Dumbrille. It was based on the novel of the same title by Harold Bell Wright.

rows.title: Calm Yourself
rows.cast: Robert Young, Madge Evans
rows.extract: Calm Yourself is a 1935 American comedy film directed by George B. Seitz and written by Arthur Kober. The film stars Robert Young, Madge Evans, Betty Furness, Ralph Morgan, Nat Pendleton and Hardie Albright. The film was released on June 28, 1935, by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.

rows.title: Cappy Ricks Returns
rows.cast: Robert McWade, Ray Walker
rows.extract: Cappy Ricks Returns is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Mack V. Wright and written by George Waggner. rows.cast: Errol Flynn, Olivia de Havilland, Lionel Atwill

rows.title: Captain Hurricane

rows.extract: Captain Hurricane is a 1935 American drama film about the life of fishermen in Cape Cod.

rows.extract: Car 99 is a 1935 American thriller film directed by Charles Barton and written by Karl Detzer and C. Gardner Sullivan. rows.title: Carnival
rows.cast: Jimmy Durante, Lee Tracy, Sally Eilers
rows.extract: Carnival is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Walter Lang and starring Jimmy Durante and Sally Eilers.

rows.cast: Warren William, Claire Dodd, Allen Jenkins
rows.extract: The Case of the Curious Bride is a 1935 American mystery film, the second in a series of four starring Warren William as Perry Mason, following The Case of the Howling Dog. rows.title: The Case of the Lucky Legs
rows.cast: Warren William, Genevieve Tobin, Patricia Ellis
rows.extract: The Case of the Lucky Legs is a 1935 mystery film, the third in a series of Perry Mason films starring Warren William as the famed lawyer.

rows.title: Case of the Missing Man
rows.cast: Roger Pryor, Joan Perry
rows.extract: The Case of the Missing Man is a 1935 American mystery crime film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Roger Pryor, Joan Perry and Thurston Hall.

rows.cast: Paul Lukas, Alison Skipworth, Rosalind Russell

rows.cast: Mary Carlisle, Hardie Albright
rows.extract: Champagne for Breakfast is a 1935 American comedy-drama film, directed by Melville Brown. It stars Mary Carlisle, Hardie Albright, and Joan Marsh, and was released on June 18, 1935.

rows.cast: Warner Oland, Rita Hayworth, Pat Paterson
rows.extract: Charlie Chan in Egypt is the eighth of 16 20th Century Fox Charlie Chan films starring Warner Oland in the title role. It was released in 1935.

rows.extract: Charlie Chan in Shanghai is the ninth Charlie Chan film produced by Fox Film Corporation with the title character played by Warner Oland.

rows.cast: Anne Shirley, O. P. Heggie, Helen Westley

rows.title: Cheers of the Crowd
rows.cast: Russell Hopton, Irene Ware
rows.extract: Cheers of the Crowd is a 1935 American drama film directed by Vin Moore and starring Russell Hopton, Irene Ware and Harry Holman.

rows.cast: Reb Russell, Victoria Vinton, Roger Williams
rows.extract: The Cheyenne Tornado is a 1935 American Western film directed by William A. O'Connor and starring Reb Russell, Victoria Vinton and Roger Williams.

rows.cast: Clark Gable, Jean Harlow, Wallace Beery
rows.extract: China Seas is a 1935 American adventure film starring Clark Gable as a brave sea captain, Jean Harlow as his brassy paramour, and Wallace Beery as a suspect character. rows.extract: Circumstantial Evidence is a 1935 drama film directed by Charles Lamont and starring Chick Chandler, Shirley Grey and Arthur Vinton.

rows.cast: Ronald Colman, Loretta Young, Colin Clive

rows.cast: Ralph Morgan, Maxine Doyle, Russell Gleason
rows.extract: Condemned to Live is a 1935 American horror film starring Ralph Morgan and Maxine Doyle, and directed by Frank R. Strayer. The film is unusual for its time, as it approaches the topic of vampirism from a sympathetic standpoint and presents it as if it were an illness.

rows.title: Confidential
rows.cast: Donald Cook, Evalyn Knapp
rows.extract: Confidential is a 1935 American crime film directed by Edward L. Cahn and written by Wellyn Totman and Olive Cooper. rows.title: Convention Girl
rows.cast: Rose Hobart, Weldon Heyburn
rows.extract: Convention Girl, also known as Atlantic City Romance, is a 1935 American comedy film starring Rose Hobart and featuring Shemp Howard of the Three Stooges. The film was directed by Luther Reed.

rows.cast: Alice White, Johnny Downs, Eddy Duchin
rows.extract: Coronado is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and written by Don Hartman and Frank Butler. It was directed by German-émigré film maker Karl Freund, and stars Peter Lorre as Dr. Gogol, Frances Drake as Yvonne Orlac and Colin Clive as Stephen Orlac. rows.title: Magnificent Obsession
rows.cast: Robert Taylor, Irene Dunne, Ralph Morgan

rows.title: Make a Million
rows.cast: Charles Starrett, Pauline Brooks, James Burke
rows.extract: Make a Million is a 1935 American film directed by Lewis D. Collins.

rows.title: Man of Iron
rows.cast: Barton MacLane, Mary Astor
rows.extract: Man of Iron is a 1935 American drama film directed by William C. McGann and written by William Wister Haines. The film stars Barton MacLane, Mary Astor, John Eldredge, Dorothy Peterson, Joseph Crehan and Craig Reynolds. The film was released by Warner Bros. on December 21, 1935.

rows.cast: W. C. Fields, Kathleen Howard, Mary Brian
rows.extract: Man on the Flying Trapeze is a 1935 American comedy film starring W. C. Fields as a henpecked husband who experiences a series of misadventures while taking a day off from work to attend a wrestling match. rows.title: The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo
rows.cast: Ronald Colman, Joan Bennett, Colin Clive
rows.extract: The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo is a 1935 American romantic comedy film made by 20th Century Fox. rows.title: Manhattan Moon
rows.cast: Ricardo Cortez, Dorothy Page, Hugh O'Connell
rows.extract: Manhattan Moon is an American romantic comedy directed by Stuart Walker, and stars Ricardo Cortez and Dorothy Page. It was released on August 5, 1935.

rows.title: Mary Burns, Fugitive
rows.cast: Sylvia Sidney, Melvyn Douglas
rows.extract: Mary Burns, Fugitive is a 1935 American drama film directed by William K. Howard.

rows.title: Mary Jane's Pa
rows.cast: Aline MacMahon, Guy Kibbee
rows.extract: Mary Jane's Pa is a 1935 American drama film directed by William Keighley and written by Tom Reed and Peter Milne. The film stars Aline MacMahon, Guy Kibbee, Tom Brown, Robert McWade, Minor Watson, and Nan Grey. The film was released by Warner Bros. on April 27, 1935.

rows.title: Maybe It's Love
rows.cast: Gloria Stuart, Ross Alexander, Ruth Donnelly

The film stars Gloria Stuart, Ross Alexander, Frank McHugh, Ruth Donnelly, Helen Lowell and Henry Travers. The film was released by Warner Bros. on January 12, 1935.

rows.title: The Melody Lingers On
rows.cast: Josephine Hutchinson, Mona Barrie
rows.extract: The Melody Lingers On is a 1935 American film.

rows.cast: Gene Autry, Ann Rutherford
rows.extract: Melody Trail is a 1935 American Western film directed by Joseph Kane and starring Gene Autry, Ann Rutherford, and Smiley Burnette. Written by Sherman L. rows.title: Men of Action
rows.cast: Frankie Darro, Edwin Maxwell, Fred Kohler
rows.extract: Men of Action is a 1935 American drama film directed by Alan James from a screenplay by Forrest Sheldon, John W. Krafft, and Barry Barringer based on Peter B. Kyne's story, "The New Freedom." The film stars Frankie Darro, Roy Mason, and Barbara Worth.

rows.cast: Lawrence Tibbett, Alice Brady, Virginia Bruce
rows.extract: Metropolitan is a 1935 back-stage drama film interlaced with songs and musical segments from opera.

rows.title: Midnight Phantom
rows.cast: Reginald Denny, Claudia Dell, Lloyd Hughes
rows.extract: Midnight Phantom is a 1935 American film directed by Bernard B. Ray.

rows.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
rows.cast: Olivia de Havilland, James Cagney, Mickey Rooney
rows.extract: A Midsummer Night's Dream is a 1935 American romantic comedy fantasy film of William Shakespeare's play, directed by Max Reinhardt and William Dieterle, and starring James Cagney, Mickey Rooney, Olivia de Havilland, Jean Muir, Joe E. Brown, Dick Powell, Ross Alexander, Anita Louise, Victor Jory and

rows.title: Million Dollar Haul
rows.cast: Reed Howes, Janet Chandler, William Farnum
rows.extract: Million Dollar Haul is a 1935 American mystery film directed by Albert Herman and starring Reed Howes, Janet Chandler and William Farnum.

rows.title: Millions in the Air
rows.cast: John Howard, Wendy Barrie
rows.extract: Millions in the Air is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Ray McCarey and written by Sig Herzig and Jane Storm. rows.title: Les Misérables
rows.cast: Charles Laughton, Fredric March, Rochelle Hudson
rows.extract: Les Misérables is a 1935 American drama film starring Fredric March and Charles Laughton based upon the 1862 Victor Hugo novel of the same name. The movie was adapted by W. P. rows.cast: Joan Blondell, Glenda Farrell, Hugh Herbert
rows.extract: Miss Pacific Fleet is a 1935 American comedy film directed by Ray Enright. The film stars Joan Blondell, Glenda Farrell, and Hugh Herbert.
